content.text: Config's latency outliers also appear in the normal period and its mean barely moved, so it looks like background noise rather than a fault. Last, I'll check how widespread station-food's slowdown is and confirm it sits in the food-service → ui-dashboard path.

input.query: SELECT 'a' p, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN duration>100000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over100, sum(CASE WHEN duration>1000000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over1s, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,1) p90 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-station-food-service' AND span_name LIKE 'POST /api%' UNION ALL SELECT 'n', count(*), sum(CASE WHEN duration>100000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN duration>1000000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-station-food-service' AND span_name LIKE 'POST /api%'

SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN duration>1000000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over1s FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('ts-food-service','ts-ui-dashboard') AND attr_span_kind='Server' AND duration>1000000000 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 4 DESC

content.text: Station-food's slow outliers are rare (one span over 1s in 114) and its p50 is unchanged, so it's a weak effect rather than a clear fault. Before deciding travel2's fault kind, I want to line up its CPU spike against the restart and the "connection refused" log burst. I'll try epoch timestamps to avoid the timezone import.

input.query: SELECT CAST(epoch_ms(time)/60000 AS BIGINT) AS minute_bucket, round(avg(CASE WHEN attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-travel2%' AND metric='container.cpu.usage' THEN value END),2) travel2_cpu, round(max(CASE WHEN attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-travel2%' AND metric='k8s.container.restarts' THEN value END),0) travel2_restarts, round(avg(CASE WHEN attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-route-plan%' AND metric='container.cpu.usage' THEN value END),3) rp_cpu FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT CAST(epoch_ms(time)/60000 AS BIGINT) AS minute_bucket, service_name, count(*) c FROM abnormal_logs WHERE level='SEVERE' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The timeline lines up: travel2 CPU spikes and the route-plan/travel-plan SEVERE burst all fall in the first abnormal minute, and travel2's restart counter rises to 1. One more check is whether food-service's error logs also cluster in that window or reflect a separate fault.

input.query: SELECT CAST(epoch_ms(time)/60000 AS BIGINT) AS minute_bucket, service_name, level, count(*) c FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND level IN ('ERROR','WARN') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Food-service's ERROR logs run through minutes 1–5, which is wider than travel2's first-minute burst, so they may be a separate effect. I'll compare the response sizes and status codes of food's outbound calls, to see whether station-food's replies changed.
